verdict.rationale: Google's own documentation describes an opt-in Privacy Screen that requires device verification (PIN, pattern or biometric) before the app can be used. That directly gates the codes behind biometrics or a PIN, so a borrowed phone doesn't expose them. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that Privacy Screen works as described, and details on which platforms support it and when it re-locks (e.g., timeout behaviour).

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app itself locks behind biometrics or a PIN, so a borrowed phone doesn't expose my codes

citations.quote: This requires a verification from your device, like a PIN, pattern or biometric prompt, before the app can be used.
